reason: Rhachis internode in grass and sedge spikes is the inflorescence axis internode. Leaf rachis internodes are rare.
Same as R2651: rachis internode is the inflorescence axis internode.
A rachis joint is the internode between two nodes of a spike rachis, as in grasses. It is the breaking point of the axis.
Same as R2653, with the rhachis spelling.
A fasciclode is a bundle of staminodes, not a single staminode. Mapping it to staminode loses the fascicle. Reject unless a fascicle term exists.
Same as R2655: a fasciclodium is a fascicle of staminodes, not one staminode.
Leaf auricle is the leaf sheath auricle only in grasses. In other plants, such as stipular, Rubus or fern auricles, the leaf base or lamina bears it.
Bare auricles also occur on stipules, corollas, bracts, pinnae and fruits. The match to PO_0020106 holds only for grass leaf and sheath contexts.
Sheath auricles are the leaf sheath auricles.
A monochasium is a cyme with one lateral branch per node. PO cyme inflorescence is the nearest class, and it also covers dichasium.
Plural of monochasium (R2660).
A spelling variant of monochasium (R2660).
A monochasial cyme is a cyme.
The limen in Passiflora is a membranous ring or cup around the base of the androgynophore, inside the coronas. It is not the corona itself. Reject unless a limen class is made.
The inner corona is only the inner part of the corona. Mapping it to floral corona loses that. Use only if no inner/outer corona classes exist.
A dyad is mostly a pair of pollen grains, or a pair of flowers or spikelets. It is not a cyme. The glossary lists it as unmapped.
Plural of dyad (R2666). Dyads are mostly pollen units, so this is not a cyme.
French dyade is a pair of pollen grains or flowers, not a cyme.
A submarginal vein runs close inside the margin of the lamina, which fits the intramarginal vein.
Plural of R2669.
French equivalent of submarginal vein (R2669).
Plural of R2671.
Sillon is a groove. PO canal lists groove and furrow as synonyms.
Plural of R2673.
Perigonial leaves are perigonial bracts only in bryophytes. In seed plants, a perigonial leaf is a tepal.
A protonemal flap is a flap-like outgrowth on the protonema, not the protonema itself. Mapping to protonema loses the part.
Same as R2676, with the other spelling.
A petiolar sheath is the sheath of a leaf at the petiole base, which maps to the leaf sheath.
Same as R2678.
French 'flore' normally means a flora, as in the book. It does not mean flower, which is 'fleur'.
'-flore' is a suffix, as in 'pauciflore' or '3-flore', meaning 'flowered'. It describes the number or kind of flowers, so it does not name a flower. Handle it as a count rule.
'-flores' is the plural suffix form ('multiflores', '3-flores'). It describes flower number, so it does not name a flower part.
The axis of a panicle is the inflorescence axis.
Plural of R2683.
The panicle rachis is the main inflorescence axis. PO lists inflorescence rachis as a synonym.
A longitudinal nerve is a vein, and PO lists vein as a synonym of vascular bundle. 'Longitudinal' is a direction and could be a separate quality.
The blade is the expanded part of a bract. Sedge and grass bracts have a sheath and a blade, so a quality of the blade would be wrongly put on the whole bract.
Same as R2687: the lamina is a part of the bract, not the whole bract.
A reduced stamen may still be fertile and just small. A staminode is sterile, so the target says more than the words do.
Same as R2689: reduced does not mean sterile.
Hyalodermis is the outer layer of hyaline cells, for example in the stem cortex of Sphagnum or on orchid roots. It is not a stem epidermis in general.
Same as R2691, with the other spelling.
Flower head is a standard name for a capitulum, and PO lists 'head' as a synonym.
Bulbils are the plural of bulbil, which is the FLOPO class.
French plural of bulbille.
French singular of bulbil.
Veinlets are the smallest veins and also occur in sepals, petals and bracts. Only for leaves does the target hold, and the smallest-order meaning is lost.
The lower surface of a leaf is the abaxial side of the lamina, covered by its abaxial epidermis.
French 'face inférieure' can be the underside of any organ. It is the leaf abaxial surface only when the bearer is a leaf, lamina, limbe or leaflet.
Lower leaf surface is the abaxial surface of the leaf lamina.
